DVI output from the OTV-S300

The OTV-S300 combines the left and right views into one output frame. Capturing that DVI output means the Mac does not need to synchronize or combine separate views.

Video processor
VISERA ELITE II · OTV-S300

Video processing and an LED light source in one unit.

Video output
DVI-D · Side-by-Side

Places the left and right views side by side in one frame.

Mac input
1 capture card

A single input contains both the left-eye and right-eye views.

Why we chose SBS output

The OTV-S300 supports both Side-by-Side and Line-by-Line output. We used SBS for this connection.

SBS keeps the two views in separate regions during compression and transmission. Compared with compressing Line-by-Line video as-is, this helps reduce color bleeding and mixing between the views. It also works with the existing Mac-to-XR streaming and display path.

Capturing and streaming a single SBS frame

Output setting
3D · Side-by-Side

We selected side-by-side output in the device menu.

Streaming settings
Resolution and frame rate

On the Mac, we adjusted the video size and target frame rate to reduce streaming latency.

Capture and streaming settings tested

  1. 2026.04.10

    720p·30fps streaming

    We captured OTV-S300 video on the Mac and selected 1280×720·30fps for live streaming. We used these settings to connect to Galaxy XR and Vision Pro.

  2. 2026.04.24

    1080p streaming

    We set capture to 1920×1080 and disabled downscaling at the sender. With these settings in the HEVC test build used at the time, Galaxy XR logs showed 1920×1080 at about 30fps.

  3. 2026.08.27

    On-site measurements with downscaled video

    We tested a single SBS input with the video size reduced to manage latency. Across stable periods under these settings, the main received resolution was 1280×720 and the average received frame rate was about 60fps.

Measurements at different streaming settings

We tested 1080p streaming in April and downscaled video at about 60fps in the operating room in August.

Planned 1920×1080 retest

We expect the “1080p original” setting to preserve a 1920×1080 input as 1920×1080 across both views, or 960×1080 per eye. At the next S300 test on site, we plan to check the input, transmitted and received resolutions.
